evidence: mux.lisp:314 fnn-mux-finish ends with `(fnn-mux-start-waiting-handshake loop)`. fnn-mux-start-waiting-handshake (841-868) calls fnn-mux-handshake-refused -> fnn-mux-finish for each :refuse, and fnn-mux-proxy-or-admit -> fnn-mux-admit -> fnn-mux-finish when fn-exp-open refuses an admitted implicit-TLS socket (1074-1077). Each of those re-enters start-waiting-handshake inside a fresh fnn-mux-guarded handler-case.
fix: Have fnn-mux-finish only mark that a slot was freed (for example, set a flag on the loop), and let fnn-mux-iterate's existing per-pass call drain the queue iteratively.
reviewer: The recursion is real. fnn-mux-finish ends with fnn-mux-start-waiting-handshake (mux.lisp:314). In its queued-socket loop, a :refuse pops the queue and calls fnn-mux-handshake-refused -> fnn-mux-finish -> start-waiting-handshake again, inside a fresh fnn-mux-guarded handler-case (mux.lisp:841-868). Consecutive refusals therefore nest. fn-hsb-admit checks the per-source budget before the slot check (books/tls-handshake-decision.lisp:336-345), so once a source's bucket is drained, all of its queued sockets are refused in one chain. The depth is bounded by the waiting cap, 32 x the in-flight limit (fn-hsb-lim-queue, tls-handshake-decision.lisp:153-155; *fn-hsb-queue-factor* = 32). That is thousands of levels at most, and whether this overflows the loop's reserved control stack depends on the profile's stack size, which I did not establish. An overflow would hit guarded's serious-condition clause and stop the service.
scenario: A loop holds a long queue of implicit-TLS sockets (up to ACL2's waiting cap) from a source whose exposure is now refused. One freed slot drains the queue as a chain: start-waiting -> guarded -> admit -> exposure refused -> finish -> start-waiting -> ... with one nesting level of several frames and a handler-case per queued socket. This is the client-driven depth growth that fnn-mux-after's comment (495-501) says lane depth-debt removed for the step path, reintroduced here for the handshake path.
title: Handshake-queue processing recurses through fnn-mux-finish, so stack depth grows with the number of consecutive refusals
